title: A sheafified Koszul coordinate is a scalar mapping cone
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, r a natural number, g:Fin(r+1)->A, i:Fin(r+1), and a in A. On X=Spec(A) [def-pc-scheme], use the category of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let P be the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] on the r generators j |-> g(i.succAbove(j)), extended by zero to cochain degrees -q. Let T be termwise associated sheaf, from cochain complexes of A-modules to cochain complexes of O_X-modules. Then the sheafified extended Koszul complex on update(g,i,a) is isomorphic, as a cochain complex, to the mapping cone of T(a times id_P). No derived-category localization, positivity, regularity, or quasi-coherence hypothesis on an auxiliary object is required.

source.place: Tags 0628 and 0629, adjoining the final generator as a scalar cone. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0629 (the TeX source is absent locally).

proof.text: Reindex the free-module basis by the permutation placing i last and sending the prefix j to i.succAbove(j). Exterior powers of this permutation commute with contraction against the reindexed sequence: check the identity on exterior-algebra scalars and extend by the left-induction Leibniz formula. This gives a Koszul complex isomorphism with the distinguished coordinate last.

For the last coordinate split exterior degree q into the prefix degree q and last-basis-vector wedge prefix degree q-1. The established tensor cone coordinates at M=A, followed by the tensor-unit isomorphism, give this decomposition and the boundary matrix (x,y) -> (d x + a*y,-d y). Degree zero has only the prefix summand. Alternatively construct the untensored maps directly from koszulLastAssembly and its bijectivity. Extend to cochain degrees -q and reorder the two summands into Mathlib mapping-cone order. The matrix equations are precisely the chain-map equations of the degreewise isomorphism, including the degree-zero boundary.

Apply the additive termwise tilde functor to the preceding complex isomorphism. Mathlib CochainComplex.mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso identifies its image cone with the cone of the mapped scalar endomorphism. Compose these two isomorphisms. This works for r=0, for zero scalars, and over the zero ring: the basis decompositions and differential equations do not assume any generator is regular or nonzero.

from.place: Perfect-generation induction step: Koszul orthogonality forces the affine restriction to be the pushforward from the smaller open; Koszul orthogonality propagates to positive powers; A sheafified Koszul coordinate is a scalar mapping cone

lean.statement: theorem koszul_coordinate_cone_iso (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (r : ℕ) (g : Fin (r + 1) → A) (i : Fin (r + 1)) (a : A) : let T := @Functor.mapHomologicalComplex ℤ (ModuleCat.{u} A) (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace)) _ _ _ _ (tilde.functor (.of A)) ⟨fun _ _ ↦ tilde.map_zero⟩ (ComplexShape.up ℤ) let P := (ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r (fun j ↦ g (i.succAbove j))).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat Nonempty (T.obj ((ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A (r + 1) (Function.update g i a)).extend ComplexShape.embeddingDownNat) ≅ CochainComplex.mappingCone (T.map (a • 𝟙 P)))
